terms.gloss: a deputy, an under-servant; here, a subagent
evidence: Hor. S. 2.7.79, Mart. 2.18.7: an under-slave kept by another slave (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Verr. 2.4.81: succēdam ego vicārius tuō mūnerī (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Classically a substitute or deputy, and especially the servant of a servant, a slave kept by another slave to do part of his work (Lewis & Short): an agent’s own helper, given a part of the task, is just that. The use is modern, and ours.

phrases.latin: Āctor vicāriōs suōs ad singula mittit.
phrases.english: The agent sends its subagents off to do the separate parts.
